title: Sentiment Analysis Variables

edits.reason: Chart title 'All Four SA Variables Aligning Bullishly at Key DBS Level' and lesson bullet 'All four bullish: ... = maximum conviction long at DBS' name the DBS level, but the def draws no markLines/markAreas at all — the DBS is only spoken. The price low/turning point is 79 (first leg .to), exactly the bar where the existing 'All 4 Aligned — Max Long!' markPoint fires (idx8); a teal DBS support line makes it locatable and matches the teal DBS convention used in this chapter's quiz.chart ('DBS Zone — All 4 SA Aligned' at yAxis:74). The squeeze tops at 117 (second leg .to) at idx15 where 'Max Confluence Target Hit' already fires; the lesson teaches 'maximum confluence' as the take-profit, so a gold target magnet at 117 turns that event pin into a locatable TP level (gold = TP/target per palette). Both yAxis values sit at the edges of the ~77-119 visible band — no clipping.

notes: Rejected auditor introChart gap 2 (markArea 77-82 'DBS Demand Zone'): redundant with the yAxis:79 DBS markLine — the auditor itself flagged it as optional/'to avoid double-drawing the same level'. Restraint: one teal level for the DBS is enough; a band would double-draw. lessonChart is genuinely complete — it is a CONCEPT chart about mixed/choppy signals and teaches NO concrete entry/stop/target levels (text: 'Mixed — Only 2/4 Signal', 'Cum Δ Indecisive', 'Win — But Not Max Size'); its 3 markPoints fully cover what it teaches, so nothing to add. quiz.chart already draws the DBS markLine (yAxis:74 teal) as the pre-cut decision context and routes all outcome events (max-conviction, max-size entry, short squeeze) to revealMarkPoints — correct slot discipline for a cutIndex:8 scenario; adding a target line near the post-cut squeeze top (113) would risk spoiling the reveal, so left untouched. Agreed with auditor that lessonChart and quiz.chart are complete; accepted 2 of the auditor's 3 introChart gaps (DBS support line + confluence target), upgrading the gold target from the auditor's 'low' confidence since it is squarely text-justified.
